drafts.walkScript: Turn to “hour”, after the gap. Its h is silent, so a vowel sound comes first, and that takes “an”. So “an hour” fits, and “a hour” clashes with that sound. “Spent hour” leaves a word out. “The hour” would mean one already named, and none has been.

Look at “Dev shrugged”, at the end. “Shrugged” tells what happened in the past, and the gap keeps step with it. So “replied” fits. “Replies” and “is replying” move the talk into now. “Has replied” does not match a story told in the past.

Start at “not rubbish”, just after the gap. Only one choice opens out into “they are”. “They are not rubbish” makes sense, so “They’re” fits. “Their” and “Theirs” show owning. “There” points at a place.

Turn to the half before the gap. “If” and “painted” picture lids that are not painted yet. An if like that takes “would”, so “would know” fits. “Will know” treats it as certain, and “would have known” looks back. “Would be knowing” is not how “know” is used.

Read either side of the gap. The joining word stands for “the girl”, the one who “never worried”. A person in that place takes “who”. “Which” is for things, and “whose” shows owning. “Whom” is for a person something is done to.

Look after the gap, at “crowd”. The gap needs a word that says what the crowd was like. The -ing form does that job, so “the cheering crowd” fits. “Cheer” and “cheers” do not describe a crowd. “Cheered” would mean the crowd was being cheered.
Turn to the sentence before the gap. Mrs Lawson wrote his time on “a board”. A board already mentioned takes “the”. “A” and “an” would bring in a new board. “Looked at board” leaves a word out.
Look at the fourth part, at “excellant”. The word “excellence” ends in -ence, and -ence goes with -ent. So an e goes where the a is, giving “excellent”. The three earlier parts hold.
Start at the first part, at the day name. Say it slowly: Wed-nes-day. The d at the end of “Wed” is missing from “Wenesday”. “Knights”, “wrote” and “hall” hold.

Go straight to the third part, at “definitely”. It is “de” plus “finite”, so the letter after the n is an i. “Wednesday” and “choir” keep their odd letters. “Separately” keeps the a of “separate”. Every part holds, so No mistake fits.
